key_insight: A Bayesian biomarker deconvolution model can separate true tissue-injury dynamics from biomarker clearance, making efficacy signals easier to infer in small uncontrolled early-phase trials.
clinical_relevance: This could help researchers estimate treatment activity and select doses in acute organ injury studies while reducing the number of participants needed.
method: Fits individual biomarker time courses with an exponentially modified Gaussian model.
Deconvolves injury kinetics from biomarker clearance.
Uses a historic cohort as a null distribution for comparison.
evidence_signal: In simulation, the framework lowered the minimum detectable treatment effect from 67.5% to 24.5% and was also applied to published case-series data to recover patient-level pharmacodynamic signatures.
watch_item: Results rely on biomarker-specific, indication-specific recalibration and on historical data quality, so performance may vary across settings and biomarkers.
paper_title: Efficacy inference in early-phase non-controlled clinical trials via Bayesian biomarker deconvolution
